recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Revisit only if Pharmacy or BR&R makes a new decision to change MedicationKnowledge scope, examples, or module indexing.
issue_request: FHIR-24101 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5 after an STU3 comment said MedicationKnowledge was unclear about whether it served medication catalogue/formulary use cases or a broader medication knowledge base. The accepted path was to clarify the Medication module and relationship boundaries rather than redesign the resource.
initial_application: The only source-history commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-24101, 2caba87573ebfebd34602aa26b0f072bd3b2b316, touched an unrelated MedicationDispense value set description. The current relevant application appears in later MedicationKnowledge and medication-definition work, especially 6422f2f98a0fcf03140c15fe93bfd6c765fc6377 and the already-published FHIR-31736 reconciliation.
additional_context: MedicationKnowledge is active in fhir.ini. Its current introduction says it supports creation and querying of medication information for formularies/catalogues, provides more detail than Medication, and is not a complete MedicinalProductDefinition. The current structure includes catalogue/formulary and clinical-support content such as costs, monitoring programs, indications, dosing guidance, classifications, packaging links, clinical issues, and storage guidance. The Medication Definition module contains the relationship-to-prescribing diagram and detailed boundary explanation, and the Medications module links readers to it.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because adding more FHIR-24101 text would duplicate current build guidance and could drift from the linked Medication Definition relationship section.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification that improved and linked documentation on how Medication, MedicationKnowledge, and Medication Definition resources work together.
Broader product-definition boundary discussion confirming MedicationKnowledge and MedicinalProductDefinition-style resources have distinct requirements rather than needing merger.
